newsitem.title: USA: USDA March 11 world grain highlights.
newsitem.headline: USDA March 11 world grain highlights.

text.p: Soybean crop prospects improved in Brazil, and the Agriculture Department increased its 1996/97 harvest forecast to 27.0 million tonnes.
USDA raised Brazil's soybean export projection to 5.20 million tonnes, up from last month's estimate of 4.20 million.

USDA left unchanged the Argentine soybean harvest at 13.5 million tonnes in its monthly report on world crops Tuesday. Argentina's soybean exports were pegged at 2.00 million tonnes, down from last month's 2.50 million tonne estimate.
China soybean imports were increased to 1.9 million tonnes, up 200,000 from last month's estimate, and China soybean production was estimated at 13.0 million tonnes, up 500,000.
World oilseed production was raised to 259.1 million tonnes due to improved soybean crops in Brazil, Paraguay and China, and increased rapeseed production in India and China.
Australia wheat exports were raised 500,000 tonnes to 17.0 million, and its production estimate was raised to 23.50 million tonnes.
World grain crops will total 1,844.07 million tonnes in 1996/97, down from last month's estimate of 1,846.63 million tonnes but above last year's 1,706.97 million.
Smaller coarse grain crops in South Africa and India were offset by larger output in Argentina, Australia and the European Union.
World wheat was pegged at 581.46 million tonnes, coarse grains at 887.74 million, rice at 374.87 million, and cotton at 86.34 million bales.
